name: os-bandwidthd
comment: Per-device bandwidth accounting, alerting and history
desc:
An OPNsense plugin around the bandwidthd capture daemon.

Adds an interactive Reporting dashboard (per-device usage, stacked top-talker
charts, 95th-percentile, per-day ledger, CSV/JSON export), a traffic alerting
engine (quota, anomaly, exfiltration and new-device rules), a multi-signal
device classifier with optional active fingerprinting, and an optional external
PostgreSQL history backend.

Device identity is keyed by MAC, so a device that changes IP through a DHCP
lease renewal stays one device.

scripts.post-install:
#!/bin/sh
# Register the new MVC controllers, ACL, menu, cron hooks and configd actions.
# The menu and ACL are read from a cache that installing files does NOT
# invalidate, so without the flush the plugin installs correctly and is simply
# absent from the navigation.
/usr/local/etc/rc.d/configd restart >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/usr/local/sbin/pluginctl -c cache_flush >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# system_cron_configure() writes the crontab; plugins_configure('cron') is a
# no-op ('cron' is not a plugin hook) and needs the full bootstrap anyway.
/usr/local/bin/php -r 'require_once("config.inc"); require_once("util.inc"); require_once("legacy_bindings.inc"); require_once("system.inc"); require_once("interfaces.inc"); require_once("plugins.inc"); system_cron_configure();' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# Render the service template so /etc/rc.conf.d/bandwidthd exists immediately;
# otherwise it only appears on the first settings save, and a reboot before
# that leaves the daemon disabled at boot.
/usr/local/sbin/configctl template reload OPNsense/Bandwidthd >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/usr/local/sbin/configctl webgui restart >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
exit 0
scripts.post-deinstall:
#!/bin/sh
# Drop this plugin's cron entries: they invoke configd actions that no longer
# exist and would keep erroring every few minutes. The hook file is already
# gone at this point, so regenerating simply omits them.
/usr/local/etc/rc.d/configd restart >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/usr/local/bin/php -r 'require_once("config.inc"); require_once("util.inc"); require_once("legacy_bindings.inc"); require_once("system.inc"); require_once("interfaces.inc"); require_once("plugins.inc"); system_cron_configure();' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
/usr/local/sbin/pluginctl -c cache_flush >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# The rendered rc.conf.d file is template output, not a package file, so pkg
# leaves it behind enabling a service that no longer exists.
rm -f /etc/rc.conf.d/bandwidthd
/usr/local/sbin/configctl webgui restart >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
exit 0
scripts.pre-deinstall:
#!/bin/sh
# Stop the daemon while the rc script this package owns still exists: pkg
# removes the package files before post-deinstall runs, so a stop there is a
# silent no-op and bandwidthd keeps capturing with nothing left to stop it.
/usr/local/etc/rc.d/bandwidthd onestop >/dev/null 2>&1 || /usr/bin/killall bandwidthd >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
exit 0
